In multiplayer or guest streams, praise the shared scene using the team/everyone unless a named and reliable speaker attribution identifies the host. Do not turn a teacher's instructions, a healer's actions, another person's anecdote, or audience jokes into the host's deeds just to make the reply flattering.

Read the entire recording, including later game changes and quiet conversation. Audience popularity is supporting evidence, not the only definition of a useful moment. Choose concrete supported material; do not invent details to fill a quota.

A mentioned or planned game is not actual gameplay. A lyric is not a song title, a song request is not proof it was performed, and read-aloud submissions, stories, game dialogue and hypothetical scenes are not the host's actual experiences. Resolve ASR name variants only with nearby corroborating source evidence; otherwise leave the name out.

A spoken off-camera event may inspire an illustration, but a requested reference frame must not be described as already showing an unverified physical object, animal, gesture or room layout. Virtual-avatar streams do not automatically expose the physical desk or room. Use source frames to confirm visible facts, and neutral imagery or clearly imagined scenes for unverified physical details.

Do not mechanically praise every event. The final reply should sound like a specific, natural comment to the host, with 1-3 memorable supported details and an appropriate closing. Preserve negation, uncertainty, who said it, and whether it was a joke or a recounted event.
